backlog.title: Bugfix: bloatThresholdFor Proto-Key Leak & Stale Spec Sync
backlog.description: Fix three minor bugs found during the P2 (Per-Tool Bloat Threshold) bug-hunt: (1) a latent prototype-key collision in bloatThresholdFor that returns Object.prototype members instead of the global threshold for tools named 'constructor'/'toString'/etc.; (2) a stale config schema in spec/04-data-model.md still showing default 8192 and missing bloatThresholdBytesByTool; (3) stale '8 KB' prose in spec/10-testing.md:67 and spec/01-pi-context-internals.md:197. All are documentation or lookup defects with low real-world impact (no built-in Pi tool triggers the proto-key path), but they contradict the shipped 16384 + {bash:32768, read:20480} configuration and violate design principle #6 (honest bookkeeping).

milestones.title: Fix BUG-001: Prototype-Key Leak in bloatThresholdFor
milestones.description: Guard the per-tool threshold lookup in src/nudges.ts so that inherited Object.prototype properties cannot masquerade as a threshold value. This is a single-function code fix with a regression test, and it transitively fixes the same defect in src/tools/audit.ts which imports bloatThresholdFor.

tasks.title: Guard bloatThresholdFor against Object.prototype key collisions
tasks.description: Add a regression test asserting bloatThresholdFor returns the global for prototype-key collision tool names ('constructor', 'toString', 'valueOf', 'hasOwnProperty'), then fix the lookup to use Object.prototype.hasOwnProperty.call before reading the value. This is TDD: write the failing test first, then implement the one-line guard.

subtasks.title: Write failing regression test + fix bloatThresholdFor hasOwnProperty guard
subtasks.context_scope:
CONTRACT DEFINITION:
1. RESEARCH NOTE: See plan/002_df93178e6631/bugfix/002_7e5972dda3a9/architecture/system_context.md §BUG-001. The function bloatThresholdFor lives at src/nudges.ts:86-91. The bug is on line ~90: `return byTool[toolName] ?? global;` — the `??` operator only catches null/undefined, not inherited Object.prototype functions. For toolName='constructor', byTool['constructor'] returns the Object constructor function, so `?? global` does NOT fall back. Downstream: `bytes < function` is always false (reminder fires on every result), and `Math.round(function/1024)` is NaN (renders '(threshold NaN KB)'). This same defect reaches src/tools/audit.ts:528 transitively — no code change needed there.
2. INPUT: The existing function signature is `bloatThresholdFor(toolName: string | undefined, config: MulliganConfig): number`. The config param is a validated MulliganConfig where config.nudges.bloatThresholdBytesByTool is a Record<string, number> (or undefined → default {}). config.nudges.bloatThresholdBytes is the global fallback (16384 in DEFAULT_CONFIG).
3. LOGIC: (A) TEST FIRST — Open test/nudges.test.ts. Find the describe block 'bloatThresholdFor — per-tool resolution' (starts ~line 136). Add a new `it(...)` test case AFTER the existing tests (after the 'respects an explicit custom override' test, before the closing `});` of the describe block). The test should: use `getConfig()` to get DEFAULT_CONFIG; assert `bloatThresholdFor('constructor', config)` returns the global `config.nudges.bloatThresholdBytes` (16384); assert the same for 'toString', 'valueOf', and 'hasOwnProperty'. The test will FAIL before the fix (returns a function, not a number). (B) FIX — In src/nudges.ts, replace the return statement `return byTool[toolName] ?? global;` with `return Object.prototype.hasOwnProperty.call(byTool, toolName) ? byTool[toolName] : global;`. Update the JSDoc comment above the function (the paragraph starting with '``byTool[toolName] ?? global`` is correct at runtime') to explain the hasOwnProperty guard prevents inherited Object.prototype members from masquerading as thresholds. Do NOT change the function signature, the `if (!toolName) return global;` early return, or the `?? {}` fallback — those are correct.
4. OUTPUT: bloatThresholdFor returns `number` for ALL string inputs (never an inherited function). The regression test passes. Run `npx vitest run test/nudges.test.ts` to verify the test passes. Run `npx vitest run test/tools/audit.test.ts` to verify no transitive regression. Run `npx tsc --noEmit` for type safety.
5. DOCS: [Mode A] Update the JSDoc on `bloatThresholdFor` in src/nudges.ts to document the hasOwnProperty guard and why it is necessary (prototype-key collision protection). No spec docs or README changes in this subtask — those are handled in P1.M2.
